wastes.name: Defects
wastes.def: Any work that has errors and must be fixed or scrapped.
wastes.example: A welded part fails inspection and goes back for rework.
wastes.fix: Build quality in at the source with checks and poka-yoke.

wastes.name: Overproduction
wastes.def: Making more, or sooner, than the customer actually needs.
wastes.example: Running a big batch 'to be efficient' that then sits in storage.
wastes.fix: Produce to real demand using pull and takt time.

wastes.name: Waiting
wastes.def: Idle time when people or products wait for the next step.
wastes.example: An operator standing idle because the previous machine is slow.
wastes.fix: Balance the line so work flows evenly between steps.

wastes.name: Non-utilized talent
wastes.def: Failing to use people's skills, ideas, and experience.
wastes.example: Ignoring the operator who knows exactly how to fix a recurring jam.
wastes.fix: Involve everyone in improvement; listen to the front line.

wastes.name: Transportation
wastes.def: Unnecessary movement of materials and products.
wastes.example: Carrying parts across the factory and back between steps.
wastes.fix: Place steps close together so products travel less.

wastes.name: Inventory
wastes.def: Excess raw material, work-in-progress, or finished goods.
wastes.example: Shelves full of stock that ties up cash and hides problems.
wastes.fix: Keep only what you need; let inventory flow, not pile up.

wastes.name: Motion
wastes.def: Unnecessary movement of people at the workstation.
wastes.example: Reaching, bending, and searching for tools every single cycle.
wastes.fix: Organize the workspace with 5S so everything is within reach.

wastes.name: Extra processing
wastes.def: Doing more work than the customer actually values.
wastes.example: Polishing a surface that will never be seen or used.
wastes.fix: Do exactly what the customer needs, no more, no less.
